transcript:
Meeting header:
- Title: Northbridge Medical - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
- Date/Time: 2027-05-12 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 55 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel, Omar Ruiz (Redwood); Sarah Kim, Tom Ellis, Anita Desai (Northbridge)

Summary: quick intro, goals, security questions, pilot scope and next steps

[00:00] Maya Patel: hi all, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll run the kickoff today, um quick round robin?
[00:12] Sarah Kim: hi maya, sarah here, head of ml ops at northbridge, thanks for setting this up
[00:18] Tom Ellis: tom, cto, i'll mainly listen and jump in on infra questions
[00:24] Anita Desai: anita from security, i have a list of questions about data residency and kms
[00:31] Maya Patel: great, and from our side omar ruiz is our solutions engineer, he'll do the deeper technical stuff, omar wave?
[00:40] Omar Ruiz: hey everyone, good to meet you, i'll take the arch deep dive later, quick note: we'll want to run a small pilot to baseline latency and cost and confirm the model quantization profile

[02:05] Maya Patel: ok goals — 1) get a shared timeline for onboarding 2) align on security requirements 3) agree pilot scope and success metrics, does that match your expectations?
[02:18] Sarah Kim: yes, and add we need to validate response time under 200ms p99 for our internal assistants and also ensure PHI never persists in logs
[02:29] Anita Desai: PHI is the big one, we need SOC2 type 2 evidence, audit logs, and customer-managed keys ideally, is that supported?
[02:45] Omar Ruiz: yes so redwood private supports customer-managed kms and we can do vpc peering for private control plane, for hosted we offer encryption at rest with our managed kms but we can also do bring-your-own-key on dedicated/private; i'll follow up with the network diagram

[05:10] Tom Ellis: about hosting options — what's the tradeoff between hosted and dedicated? cost/perf wise and operations?
[05:22] Maya Patel: hosted is fastest to get started, usage-based pricing; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, reserved capacity usually has lower unit cost at scale and gives you KMS options and VPC; private on-prem is also possible for air-gapped needs
[05:40] Sarah Kim: for our first phase, we prefer dedicated in a VPC in our preferred cloud region, we want to avoid egress latencies, is that possible?
[05:52] Omar Ruiz: yes we can provision dedicated pools in your region — there is a lead time for reserving GPU capacity, typically 2-4 weeks depending on size; we'll include options in the SOW

[08:12] Anita Desai: about logging — we need audit logs for model inference and key access, retention controls, and the ability to disable request logging for specific endpoints handling PHI, does redwood support that?
[08:28] Omar Ruiz: we have per-route logging controls and redwood console allows you to set retention policies and redact payloads; for PHI we recommend the private deployment path where logs stay in your VPC and you can forward to your SIEM

[10:00] Sarah Kim: excellent, also curious on model versions and rollback. we need predictable rollouts and the ability to pin a model version for a route
[10:10] Maya Patel: yes, rollouts are supported, can do canary and A/B, and pin model versions per route in config; we also have automatic fallback policies to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained

[12:30] Tom Ellis: performance — how do you handle kv cache and batching, we worry about cold-cache latency for sparse queries
[12:45] Omar Ruiz: runtime uses continuous batching and kv cache management; for cold-starts we suggest warmers and caching prefixes, and we can tune sequence length cutoffs and quantization profiles to balance latency/cost; we'll capture your traffic distribution in the benchmark plan

[15:02] Sarah Kim: on the topic of benchmarks, can we do a 2-week pilot that runs our sample queries and measures p99 latency and cost per 1M tokens?
[15:12] Omar Ruiz: absolutely, typical pilot: provision a dedicated test pool, run your sample set, we'll collect token counts, latency percentiles, and suggest quantization/batching settings to meet your SLOs

[17:40] Anita Desai: security paperwork — we need vendor SOC2, encryption details, SAML SSO support, SCIM for provisioning, and contractual terms for data residency. who owns that?
[17:53] Maya Patel: i'll own the SOC2 and vendor pack, omar will provide the network / architecture diagram, and legal will send the security addendum; i'll put the docs link in a follow-up email

[20:05] Tom Ellis: integration points — we plan to call Redwood's REST API from our backend and use embeddings for semantic search. do you have SDKs?
[20:15] Omar Ruiz: yes, we have python and typescript SDKs and a REST API; for embeddings we have per-unit billing; we recommend using the SDK for streaming and function calls if you need lower latencies

[23:00] Sarah Kim: data handling — we need to ensure requests with PHI are not retained; is there a toggle to disable retention?
[23:10] Omar Ruiz: for hosted customers, data retention can be restricted and redwood offers a data-retention flag per request; for private/dedicated we can ensure logs are not shipped and retention is controlled in your environment

[25:34] Anita Desai: about key management, do you integrate with AWS KMS and our HSM?
[25:40] Omar Ruiz: yes, we support AWS KMS and can integrate with customer HSMs in private deployments; we'll need to map required key rotation policies in the SOW

[28:50] Maya Patel: timeline proposal: week 0: SOW and security review; week 1-2: provision dedicated test pool and run pilot; week 3: review results and finalize production switchover plan, does that work?
[29:03] Sarah Kim: sounds reasonable, assuming the SOW includes capacity and cost estimates for our expected 50k qps monthly token volume
[29:15] Maya Patel: we'll include an estimate and a couple of capacity tiers, and options for autoscale/bursting

[32:20] Tom Ellis: contract/commercial questions — how do overage and burst credits work?
[32:28] Maya Patel: overage rates are documented in the SOW, dedicated reserves come with burst capacity options; we'll include examples in the pricing appendix

[34:50] Sarah Kim: any concerns about model hallucinations for our assistive workflows? we need guardrails and evaluation sets
[34:58] Omar Ruiz: we recommend evals tied to your prompt sets; Redwood Optimize can run simulated workloads and give quality/regression alerts; part of pilot we'll run a small eval harness against your golden set

[37:30] Anita Desai: legal — we'll need DPA and standard contractual clauses for EU data if any of our users are in EMEA
[37:40] Maya Patel: legal will include DPA and SCCs if needed; i'll flag EMEA residency requirements in the request

[40:05] Maya Patel: ok recap of owners: maya will send SOW and SOC2 pack, omar will schedule se deep-dive and provide network diagram and benchmark plan, sarah will send sample dataset and expected query profiles, anita will send compliance matrix
[40:22] Sarah Kim: yes we'll send dataset and a short doc describing expected traffic patterns and SLOs

[42:00] Tom Ellis: one last infra question — do you support private peering and direct connect to reduce latency?
[42:10] Omar Ruiz: yes, VPC peering and direct connect are supported in the private/dedicated flows, we'll detail ports and peering steps in the network diagram

[45:30] Anita Desai: onboarding checklist for security — i'd like to see penetration test cadence, incident response contacts, and how keys are rotated
[45:40] Maya Patel: noted, i'll include pen test cadence, incident response contacts, and the KMS rotation policy in the docs pack

[48:00] Sarah Kim: timeline acceptance — when can we start the pilot?
[48:10] Maya Patel: if we sign SOW by 2027-05-16 and provision resource the following week we can start pilot on 2027-05-24
[48:22] Tom Ellis: that aligns with our internal timelines

[50:00] Maya Patel: any other questions?
[50:05] Sarah Kim: none from me, thanks everyone
[50:10] Tom Ellis: good meeting, thanks
[50:13] Anita Desai: thanks, bye

[50:20] Maya Patel: thanks folks, i'll send the follow-ups and schedule the deep-dive, bye

Action items listed above, next steps agreed. End of transcript.
